reading.body:
CoreSite VA3 publishes 533,000 square feet of technical space but no IT load figure in megawatts. Without a published power number, it is not possible to translate this campus into rack counts or accelerator estimates, and doing so would require inventing a number the operator has not disclosed. The footprint alone is large, enough that power capacity is almost certainly substantial, but "almost certainly" is not a published fact.

The six certifications shape what the campus can host. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 qualify it for workloads where financial or operational audit trails are required. ISO 27001 qualifies it for workloads under formal information security management mandates. NIST 800-53 qualifies it for workloads aligned to U.S. federal security controls. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card data. HIPAA qualifies it for protected health information. None of those certifications are specific to AI training density, but they make the campus eligible for regulated AI inference or data processing workloads that carry compliance requirements.

Virginia leads U.S. data center density by any reasonable measure, and this site's state context records 326 mapped facilities and 1,326 MW of published capacity across 19 facilities that have disclosed a number. VA3 ranks twentieth by published megawatts, which in this context means it did not publish a megawatt figure at all, placing it outside the 19 facilities that did. That tells a reader that VA3 sits in the most competitive data center market in the country, and that its operator has chosen not to publish the power specification that would let anyone assess its AI scaling relevance directly.
